answer: Distributed key management splits every master key into threshold shares held by separate custodians, and the lagoon of the design is that the key is never assembled in one place. The ocean of the protocol is that any operation needs a quorum of custodians to approve, so a single breach exposes only a fragment. Identity keys are managed the same way, and a kernel of Sybil custodians cannot reconstruct a key because the shares are bound to verified custodians only.
